ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two lines \( {l}_{1} \) and \( {l}_{2} \) passing through point \(A(1, 0)\) intersect the y-axis at points \(B\) and \(C\) respectively, where point \(B\) is above the origin and point \(C\) is below the origin. It is known that \( AB = \sqrt{10} \). If the area of \( \triangle ABC \) is 3, what is the equation of line \( {l}_{2} \)?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, two lines \(l_1\) and \(l_2\) passing through point \(A(1, 0)\) intersect the y-axis at points \(B\) and \(C\) respectively, where point \(B\) is above the origin and point \(C\) is below the origin. It is known that \(AB = \sqrt{10}\). If the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is 3, what is the equation of line \(l_2\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is 3, it follows that \(\frac{1}{2}BC \cdot AO = 3\). Hence, \(\frac{1}{2}BC \times 1 = 3\), which implies \(BC=6\). Since \(BO=3\), it follows that \(CO=3\). Therefore, the coordinates of point C are \((0, -3)\). Let the equation of line \(l_2\) be \(y = kx + b\) (\(k \neq 0\)). We then have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=-3 \\ k+b=0 \end{array} \right. \] Solving this system of equations, we obtain \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k=3 \\ b=-3 \end{array} \right. \] Thus, the equation of the line \(l_2\) is \(y=3x-3\). Therefore, the answer is \(\boxed{y=3x-3}\).
